title: Linked List Cycle
keyIdea: Two pointers: slow moves 1 node, fast moves 2. No cycle → fast reaches NULL. Cycle → inside the loop fast gains 1 node per step on slow, so they must meet.

approaches.name: Hash set of visited nodes
approaches.idea: Walk the list; a node already in the set means a cycle; NULL means none.
approaches.why: Each node visited once, but the set stores them all.

approaches.name: Fast and slow pointers (Floyd)
approaches.idea: slow = slow->next, fast = fast->next->next while fast and fast->next exist; equal → true.
approaches.why: fast reaches the end, or catches slow within one lap of the cycle.

quiz.q: Why must fast and slow meet if there is a cycle?
options: Inside the cycle the gap shrinks by exactly 1 each step, so it reaches 0 without jumping over it
fast jumps two nodes; fast->next->next would crash if fast->next were NULL

quiz.q: Why compare nodes (fast == slow), not values?
options: Different nodes can hold the same value

quiz.q: Space of the hash-set version vs Floyd?
